rationale: A reference link's destination lives in a `link_reference_definition` at BLOCK level, so the companion inline grammar gives only the LABEL. Before this fixture the whole form produced no `uses` edge at all -- 671 sites (44 uses + 627 definitions) across 66 of the lane's 738 corpus files -- while the lane doc claimed 'Links (inline and reference destinations)'. Four shapes are pinned: the three reference forms resolve to the DESTINATION the document declares; an inline link and both autolink forms still resolve; a link inside a code span or a closed fence is NOT published, and that exclusion is structural rather than filtered (the inline grammar gives `code_span` only ANONYMOUS children, so a `link_destination` is unreachable beneath one); and an UNDEFINED reference is deliberately not published, because CommonMark renders it as literal text. The last one is a decision with a measurement behind it: publishing the undefined case produced 171 edges in 34 corpus files, sampled and found to be dominated by bare bracketed citation markers (`NOTICE.md: document -> 1`, six times), so those edges were fabricated endpoints and R10 target-spelling violations.

expectRelationships.from: A code span, and a closed code fence, are not links

forbidRelationships.comment: a link inside a code span is not a link. Target-only, no `from`: the defect is that this DESTINATION is published at all, and pinning the owner would make the assertion depend on the walk's attribution instead of on the exclusion. `expectRelationships` treats unspecified fields as wildcards.
an UNDEFINED reference is literal text per CommonMark, not a link
a bare bracketed citation marker is not a reference link; measured at 171 such edges over 34 corpus files when this was published

_measuredOnTheLaneCorpus.note: the numbers the fix is accountable for, re-derivable against the same pin

_declaredLimitation.what: An undefined reference link is INVISIBLE, not flagged. A reader cannot distinguish 'this document has a broken reference' from 'this document never had one'.
_declaredLimitation.why: The alternative measured as 171 fabricated endpoints over 34 corpus files, dominated by bare bracketed citation markers. Publishing them would make the graph lie; the honest options were to publish nothing or to invent a suppression heuristic, and a heuristic with no evidence behind it is the thing this repository forbids most loudly.
_declaredLimitation.wouldBeWrongTo: restore the undefined case without a corpus measurement showing the citation-marker class is gone
